section_summary.extract_value: This Discussion summarizes a single cross-sectional study using an online sample that found body appreciation was the strongest predictor of multiple indices of hedonic and eudaimonic well-being, with BMI negatively associated with well-being. The authors note limitations including reliance on cross-sectional, online recruitment (possible higher education and female recruitment biases), small non-White subsamples, and some improbable self-reported BMI values, and recommend longitudinal and more diverse future work.
section_summary.evidence_source: In the present study, we examined associations between multiple facets of positive body image and indices of hedonic and eudaimonic well-being. A further limitation of the present study was the reliance on an online sample, which may limit the generalizability of our findings (e.g., our sample may have been over-represented in terms of higher education compared with the general population). In addition, some participants returned data with improbable BMI values.
